newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on setback, hedging.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on setback, hedging.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on a profit-taking setback, hedge selling and on position squaring, traders said.
"After a long week of fund buying it's taking a break," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Funds bought roughly 40 million bushels of soybeans Thursday but the CBOT's final open interest figures showed a decline Thursday of 250,000 bushels.
Many traders were expecting the open interest to increase due to the heavy volume of fund and other speculative demand Thursday.
"The biggest surprise was the lack of an increase in open interest yesterday. There was more commercial selling and farm selling yesterday than I thought," a trader said.
Soybeans were underpinned by a continued strong weekly soybean crush pace and on remnants of Wednesday's bullish USDA supply/demand report, the traders said.
Positioning was noted before the release late Friday of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report and prior to the three-day holiday weekend.
Soybeans closed 1-3/4 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 4-1/2 at $7.61.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 50,000 contracts, well below the 77,085 traded Thursday.

In soybean options, Term Commodities bought 1,400 March $7.50 puts at 2-1/2 to 2-3/4 cents, ING Derivatives bought 600 May $7.75 calls at 18-1/2 cents and Cargill Investor Services sold 400 March $7.75 puts at 15 to 16 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, below the 32,939 traded Thursday.
